mainTopic: Aggadot on צדיקים and the 'אבירי לב', the חתן and יוהרא contradiction, and the opening of פרק מי שמתו on exemptions for an אונן
overview: The amud opens by finishing the explanation of the פסוק 'אין פרץ ואין יוצאת ואין צווחה ברחובותינו'. Each phrase is read as a prayer that our students not turn bad like אחיתופל, דואג, גחזי, or ישו הנוצרי. Next comes the פסוק 'שמעו אלי אבירי לב הרחוקים מצדקה'. Two views read it as praise of צדיקים, one supported by the בת קול about חנינא בן דוסא. רב יהודה instead says it means stubborn people who never convert, and רב יוסף and רב אשי give examples. The גמרא then returns to the משנה about a חתן reading קריאת שמע. It raises a contradiction about יוהרא from the משנה on working on תשעה באב. רבי יוחנן answers by switching the names, and רב שישא answers by explaining the difference between the cases. The chapter ends with a הדרן. Then פרק מי שמתו begins: the משנה rules who is exempt from קריאת שמע and other מצוות around a funeral, and which מצוות apply to נשים, עבדים, and קטנים. Finally, the גמרא infers that the mourner is exempt only when the body is before him, and challenges this with a ברייתא. The discussion of that challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: No breach: not like דוד's group with אחיתופל
steps.stepSummary: The phrase 'אין פרץ' is read as a prayer that our group should not produce someone like אחיתופל, who came out of דוד's circle.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'There is no breach' means: may our group not be like the group of דוד, from which אחיתופל came out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is continuing its phrase-by-phrase explanation of the פסוק. It explains the words 'אין פרץ'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A 'breach' is a crack in a wall. Here it stands for a person who breaks away from inside the group. אחיתופל was דוד's own advisor, yet he turned against him and joined אבשלום's rebellion. The prayer asks that no such traitor come out of our circle of students.

keyTerms.meaning: A breach or crack in a wall

phrases.english: "There is no breach"
that our group should not be
like the group of David
from which Achitofel came out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the phrase-by-phrase reading of the פסוק that began on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'אין פרץ' is a prayer that no traitor like אחיתופל should come out of our group.

steps.title: No going out: not like שאול's group with דואג
steps.stepSummary: The phrase 'ואין יוצאת' is read as a prayer that our group should not produce someone like דואג האדומי, who came out of שאול's circle.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And no going out' means: may our group not be like the group of שאול, from which דואג האדומי came out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the next words in the פסוק, 'ואין יוצאת'. It uses the same pattern as before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Going out' hints at someone who goes out onto a bad path. דואג was a leading figure in שאול's court. He informed on the כהנים of נוב and then killed them. The prayer asks that none of our people go out to such evil.

keyTerms.meaning: Going out, read here as going out to a bad path
דואג האדומי, a figure in שאול's court who caused the killing of the כהנים of נוב

phrases.english: "And no going out"
that our group should not be
like the group of Saul
from which Doeg the Edomite came out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next phrase of the same פסוק, using the same pattern.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'ואין יוצאת' is a prayer that no one like דואג should come out of our group.

steps.title: No outcry: not like אלישע's group with גחזי
steps.stepSummary: The phrase 'ואין צווחה' is read as a prayer that our group should not produce someone like גחזי, the student of אלישע.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And no outcry' means: may our group not be like the group of אלישע, from which גחזי came out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the third phrase, 'ואין צווחה', using the same pattern.
steps.deeperAnalysis: גחזי was אלישע's personal attendant and student. He went bad: he took payment from נעמן against his teacher's wishes, and he was punished with צרעת. The prayer asks that no student of ours turn out like him.

phrases.english: "And no outcry"
that our group should not be
like the group of Elisha
from which Gehazi came out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third phrase of the same פסוק, using the same pattern.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'ואין צווחה' is a prayer that no student like גחזי should come out of our group.

steps.title: In our streets: no child or student who sins in public
steps.stepSummary: The word 'ברחובותינו' is read as a prayer that we should not have a son or student who ruins things in public, like ישו הנוצרי.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'In our streets' means: may we not have a son or a student who burns his food in public, such as ישו הנוצרי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the last word of the phrase, 'ברחובותינו', and finishes the explanation of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Streets' means a public place. 'Burning his food in public' is a picture for sinning openly and leading many others astray. The example given is ישו הנוצרי, whom the גמרא describes as a student who went bad publicly.

keyTerms.meaning: In our streets, meaning in public
Burns his food, a picture for sinning or spoiling things
In public, in front of many people

steps.whatToRemember: Each phrase of 'אין פרץ ואין יוצאת ואין צווחה ברחובותינו' is a prayer that the בית מדרש should not produce a student who goes bad: אחיתופל, דואג, גחזי, and someone who sins publicly.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Burns his food' is not about cooking. It is an image for spoiling things or sinning in public.

phrases.english: "In our streets"

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא לָנוּ בֵּן אוֹ תַּלְמִיד
phrases.english: that we should not have a son or student
who burns his food in public,
phrases.notes: An image for sinning openly and causing others to sin

phrases.english: such as Yeshu the Notzri.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״בִּרְחוֹבוֹתֵינוּ״ — שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא לָנוּ בֵּן אוֹ תַּלְמִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final word of the פסוק, which finishes this reading.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'ברחובותינו' is a prayer that we not have a child or student who sins publicly.

steps.title: A new verse: the first view says the righteous are sustained by right
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a new פסוק with a similar dispute. One opinion says the world is fed through ה׳'s kindness, but the צדיקים are fed 'by force' because they earned it.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Listen to Me, stubborn-hearted ones who are far from צדקה.' רב and שמואל argued about this, and some say it was רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר. One said: the whole world is fed through צדקה, and they (the צדיקים) are fed by force.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new פסוק in ישעיה because it has the same kind of dispute: רב and שמואל, or else רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר. The first opinion is stated here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this reading the 'אבירי לב' are strong-hearted צדיקים. They are 'far from צדקה' because they do not need ה׳'s free kindness. Everyone else is fed as a free gift, but the צדיקים are fed 'בזרוע', meaning by right, because their good deeds earned it.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say, introducing a different version of who said it
By force, meaning by right that they earned

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'אבירי לב' and 'far from צדקה' are praise, not criticism. They describe צדיקים who do not need free kindness, not wicked people.

phrases.english: "Listen to Me, stubborn-hearted ones
who are far from charity"
Rav and Shmuel argued about this,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר.
phrases.english: and some say it was Rabbi Yochanan and Rabbi Elazar.
One said:
the whole world is fed through charity,
and they are fed by force.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״שִׁמְעוּ אֵלַי אַבִּירֵי לֵב הָרְחוֹקִים מִצְּדָקָה״, רַב וּשְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new פסוק that is linked to the previous one only because it has the same pair of disputing אמוראים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: First view: the world is fed through ה׳'s kindness, while the צדיקים are fed by their own merit.

steps.title: The second view says the world is fed in the merit of the righteous
steps.stepSummary: The other opinion says the whole world is fed in the merit of the צדיקים, while the צדיקים themselves are not even fed in their own merit. This matches a teaching of רב יהודה in the name of רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one said: the whole world is fed in their merit, and they are not fed even by their own merit. This is like what רב יהודה said in the name of רב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second opinion. It then sets up the next step by saying this view matches a statement of רב יהודה in the name of רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here 'far from צדקה' means the צדיקים are far from receiving good themselves. Their merit feeds everyone else, yet they live with very little. The phrase 'כדרב יהודה אמר רב' announces that a supporting source is about to be quoted.

keyTerms.meaning: Like the teaching of רב יהודה

phrases.english: And one said:
the whole world is fed in their merit,
and they, even in their own merit,
are not fed.
This is like what Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְחַד אָמַר: כָּל הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ נִזּוֹנִין בִּזְכוּתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second side of the dispute begun in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Second view: the world is fed in the merit of the צדיקים, while they themselves receive almost nothing.

steps.title: The heavenly voice about חנינא בן דוסא
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes רב: every day a בת קול says that the whole world is fed because of חנינא בן דוסא, yet he lives on a קב of carobs from one Friday to the next.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב יהודה said in the name of רב: every single day a בת קול goes out from הר חורב and says, 'The whole world is fed because of חנינא My son, and חנינא My son is satisfied with a קב of carobs from one ערב שבת to the next ערב שבת.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the teaching of רב יהודה in the name of רב, which shows the second opinion in a real-life example.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא בן דוסא is a perfect picture of the second view. His merit fed the whole world, while he himself had only a small measure of cheap carobs for a full week. So the צדיק supports everyone and is 'far from' receiving good himself.

keyTerms.meaning: A קב (a small measure) of carobs
From one Friday to the next, meaning a whole week

steps.whyThisMatters: This well-known statement shows that a צדיק's merit can support the whole world even while he lives in poverty.

phrases.english: As Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav:
every single day

phrases.aramaic: בַּת קוֹל יוֹצֵאת מֵהַר חוֹרֵב וְאוֹמֶרֶת:
phrases.english: a heavenly voice goes out from Mount Horeb and says:
the whole world is fed
because of Chanina My son,

phrases.aramaic: וַחֲנִינָא בְּנִי דַּי לוֹ בְּקַב חָרוּבִין
phrases.english: and Chanina My son is satisfied with a kav of carobs
from one Shabbat eve to the next Shabbat eve.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the source referred to by 'כדרב יהודה אמר רב'.
steps.raayaObject: The second view, that the world is fed in the merit of צדיקים who receive little themselves.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב יהודה in the name of רב: the בת קול about חנינא בן דוסא.

steps.title: רב יהודה's own view: the stubborn-hearted are the fools of גובאי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that this whole approach argues with רב יהודה, who says the 'אבירי לב' are the foolish people of גובאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this disagrees with רב יהודה. For רב יהודה said: who are the 'stubborn-hearted'? The foolish people of גובאי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that both opinions above disagree with רב יהודה's reading of the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both earlier opinions read 'אבירי לב' as praise for צדיקים. רב יהודה reads it as an insult: stubborn, foolish non-Jews from a place called גובאי. 'Far from צדקה' would then mean far from righteousness.
steps.confusionAlert: רב יהודה here is the same רב יהודה whose quote of רב was used in step 7. In his own reading of this פסוק, he takes a completely different direction.

phrases.english: And this disagrees with Rav Yehuda.
For Rav Yehuda said:
who are the "stubborn-hearted"?
The foolish people of Gova.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts the readings in steps 5 and 6 with a completely different reading.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רב יהודה, 'אבירי לב' refers to the foolish, stubborn people of גובאי, not to צדיקים.

steps.title: רב יוסף's proof: no convert ever came from them
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף supports רב יהודה's reading: you can see the people of גובאי are stubborn-hearted, because not one of them has ever converted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Know that this is true, because not a single convert has ever converted from among them.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף brings a proof that backs up רב יהודה's reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If even one person from גובאי had joined the Jewish people, they would not be fully 'stubborn-hearted'. The fact that none ever converted shows their hearts are completely closed. So they fit the description 'אבירי לב הרחוקים מצדקה' perfectly.

keyTerms.meaning: Know it, a word that introduces a proof

steps.whatToRemember: There are three readings of 'אבירי לב'. One: צדיקים who are fed by right. Two: צדיקים whose merit feeds the world while they have little, like חנינא בן דוסא. Three, רב יהודה's view: the foolish people of גובאי, supported by רב יוסף because none of them ever converted.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
Know that this is true, because there has never converted
a single convert from among them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב יהודה's reading from step 8.
steps.raayaObject: רב יהודה's reading that the 'אבירי לב' are the people of גובאי.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The fact, noted by רב יוסף, that no one from גובאי ever converted.

steps.title: The people of מתא מחסיא are also stubborn-hearted
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי gives a parallel example of 'אבירי לב': the people of מתא מחסיא see the glory of Torah twice a year and still none of them converts.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: The people of מתא מחסיא are 'stubborn-hearted.' They see the honor of Torah twice a year, and still not one of them has ever converted.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי adds his own example to רב יוסף's point about the people of גובאי. He names his own town, מתא מחסיא, as another place whose people are 'אבירי לב.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Twice a year, crowds gathered in מתא מחסיא to learn Torah at the כלה gatherings in אדר and אלול. The non-Jews there saw this honor of Torah up close. If even that never moved one of them to convert, they fit the meaning of 'stubborn-hearted' in רב יהודה's reading of the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: The town of רב אשי's ישיבה

steps.whatToRemember: The aggadah ends here. Both רב יוסף (about גובאי) and רב אשי (about מתא מחסיא) support רב יהודה: 'אבירי לב' means people who see greatness and are still not moved by it.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
The people of the town Mata Mechasya
are the 'stubborn-hearted',
for they see the glory of the Torah
two times a year,
and not a single convert converts from among them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: בְּנֵי מָתָא מַחְסֵיָא ״אַבִּירֵי לֵב״ נִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallels רב יוסף's support in Step 9 with a second example.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The people of מתא מחסיא are 'אבירי לב', because they see the honor of Torah twice a year and none of them converts.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: a חתן who wants to read קריאת שמע
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: a חתן who wants to read קריאת שמע on his wedding night may do so.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'A groom, if he wants to read [קריאת שמע], he may...' and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the aggadah and goes back to the משנה. It quotes the line about a חתן, which sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, a חתן is exempt from קריאת שמע on his first night. The רבנן say he may still read it if he wants to. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says he may not, because not everyone may act like the spiritual elite; doing so looks like יוהרא.

keyTerms.meaning: If he wishes to read (קריאת שמע)
Etc.: the rest of the משנה is assumed

phrases.english: A groom, if he wishes to read [Shema], etc.
phrases.notes: The 'etc.' points to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's opposing view

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic. The גמרא returns from the aggadah to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The רבנן let a חתן read קריאת שמע if he wants. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל forbids it because of יוהרא.

steps.title: But elsewhere they hold the opposite about showing off
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: does this mean רבן שמעון בן גמליאל worries about יוהרא and the רבנן do not? We have learned that they hold the reverse!
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this mean that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is worried about showing off, and the רבנן are not? But we have heard them say the opposite!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states what the משנה seems to show about each side's view on יוהרא. Then it announces that another source shows the reverse. The proof comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From our משנה, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל seems to care about יוהרא, and the רבנן seem not to. The גמרא says another משנה flips this. That would make each side contradict itself.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say...? (introduces a conclusion the גמרא is about to question)
Showing off / acting more pious than others

phrases.english: Is that to say that Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel
is concerned about showing off
and the Rabbis are not concerned about showing off?
But we have heard them [hold] the opposite!

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמֵימְרָא דְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל חָיֵישׁ לְיוּהֲרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the positions implied by the משנה quoted in Step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view on יוהרא implied for each side in the חתן משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each side seems to hold the reverse view on יוהרא in another משנה, so their positions look inconsistent.

steps.title: The משנה about working on תשעה באב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the משנה about working on תשעה באב. The רבנן say only תלמידי חכמים refrain everywhere. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says anyone may act like a תלמיד חכם.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: In a place where people work on תשעה באב, they work. In a place where they don't work, they don't work. And in every place, תלמידי חכמים stop working. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: Every person may always make himself like a תלמיד חכם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source that shows the 'opposite.' It is a משנה about whether people stop working on תשעה באב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן let only תלמידי חכמים stop working in a town where people work. So they seem to worry that an ordinary person doing it would look like יוהרא. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל lets anyone act like a תלמיד חכם, so here he does not seem to worry about יוהרא. That is the reverse of their views in the חתן case.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
A place where the custom is

steps.confusionAlert: Watch who is lenient about what. In the חתן case, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is the one who says 'don't do it, it's showing off.' In the תשעה באב case, he is the one who says 'anyone may do it.'

phrases.english: As we learned [in a Mishnah]:
A place where they were accustomed to do work
on the Ninth of Av, they work.

phrases.aramaic: מָקוֹם שֶׁנָּהֲגוּ שֶׁלֹּא לַעֲשׂוֹת — אֵין עוֹשִׂין.
phrases.english: A place where they were accustomed not to work, they do not work.
And in every place, Torah scholars are idle.
phrases.notes: Only scholars, which implies ordinary people would be showing off

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
A person may always make
himself like a Torah scholar.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: מָקוֹם שֶׁנָּהֲגוּ לַעֲשׂוֹת מְלָאכָה בְּתִשְׁעָה בְּאָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source behind the claim 'we heard them say the opposite' in Step 12.
steps.raayaObject: That the רבנן worry about יוהרא and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל does not
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about working on תשעה באב

steps.title: Each side contradicts itself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states the double contradiction: the רבנן against the רבנן, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל against רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a contradiction between the רבנן and the רבנן. There is a contradiction between רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sums up the challenge. Both sides seem to contradict themselves between the two משניות. The answer will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן ignore יוהרא for the חתן but worry about it on תשעה באב. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל worries about יוהרא for the חתן but ignores it on תשעה באב. The גמרא now needs to explain how each side can hold both views.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic 'סתירה' (internal contradiction). The usual way to answer it is to find a real difference between the two cases. Here, that means a difference between reading קריאת שמע and refraining from work.

phrases.english: There is a contradiction between the Rabbis and the Rabbis,
there is a contradiction between Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel
and Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: States the formal contradiction that comes out of the proof in Step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: How consistent each side is about יוהרא across the two משניות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each side's view on showing off flips between the חתן case and the תשעה באב case.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: The names are switched
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers the double contradiction by saying the names of who holds what must be reversed in one of the sources.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: The opinions are switched.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a first, quick answer to the contradiction from Step 14. In one of the two משניות, the names of the opinions must be swapped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the names are flipped, the רבנן are consistent in both cases and so is רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. The contradiction disappears. The cost is that we have to change which name goes with which opinion in one of the sources.

keyTerms.meaning: the line of opinions (who holds what)
showing off, acting more pious than others

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
The opinions are switched.
phrases.notes: In one of the sources, swap which opinion belongs to the רבנן and which to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the double contradiction raised in Step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual emendation: reversing the attribution of opinions
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רבנן and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל each seemed to flip their view on יוהרא between the two cases.
steps.terutzMaskana: The names in one source are reversed, so each side holds one consistent view.

steps.title: רב שישא: No switch needed, and the רבנן are consistent
steps.stepSummary: רב שישא בריה דרב אידי says we do not need to switch the names. The רבנן are consistent because a חתן reading שמע does not stand out, while not working on תשעה באב does stand out.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שישא בריה דרב אידי said: Really, do not switch the names. The רבנן do not contradict themselves. With קריאת שמע, everyone is reading it and he is reading it too, so it does not look like showing off. Here, on תשעה באב, everyone is working and he is not working, so it looks like showing off.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שישא gives a second answer that keeps the משניות as they are. He starts by solving the first half of the contradiction: the רבנן against the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The test for יוהרא is whether the person stands out from the crowd. When a חתן says קריאת שמע, he does what everyone else is doing, so nobody notices. When someone refuses to work on תשעה באב while everyone else works, he is visibly different, so it looks like showing off.

keyTerms.meaning: really / in truth (keeping the original reading)

steps.confusionAlert: The רבנן do care about יוהרא in both places. The difference is that in the חתן case nothing stands out, so there is no יוהרא to worry about.

phrases.aramaic: רַב שִׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי אָמַר:
phrases.english: Rav Sheisha son of Rav Idi said:
Really, do not switch the names.
The Rabbis against the Rabbis is not difficult:

phrases.aramaic: קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע, כֵּיוָן דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא קָא קָרוּ
phrases.english: With the reading of Shema, since everyone is reading it

phrases.aramaic: וְאִיהוּ נָמֵי קָרֵי — לָא מִיחְזֵי כְּיוּהֲרָא.
phrases.english: and he is reading it too, it does not look like showing off.

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא, כֵּיוָן דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא עָבְדִי מְלָאכָה
phrases.english: Here (Tisha B'Av), since everyone is doing work

phrases.aramaic: וְאִיהוּ לָא קָא עָבֵיד — מִיחְזֵי כְּיוּהֲרָא.
phrases.english: and he is not working, it looks like showing off.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer from רבי יוחנן, keeping the original names and making a distinction between the cases.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רבנן ignore יוהרא for the חתן but worry about it on תשעה באב, so they seem inconsistent.
steps.terutzMaskana: יוהרא depends on standing out. A חתן reading שמע blends in. Someone not working on תשעה באב stands out.

steps.title: רב שישא: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is consistent too
steps.stepSummary: For רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, the חתן case depends on כוונה, and everyone knows a חתן cannot concentrate. On תשעה באב, people will just think the idle man has no work.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל against רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is not difficult. There, the matter depends on כוונה, and we all can testify that he cannot focus his mind. But here, someone who sees him says: he simply has no work. Go out and see how many idle people there are in the marketplace.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שישא now solves the second half of the contradiction and shows that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is also consistent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a חתן, קריאת שמע requires כוונה, and it is obvious that a nervous groom cannot focus. So his reading looks like pretending, which is יוהרא. On תשעה באב, an idle person does not look pious at all, since plenty of people sit idle in the market anyway. So there is no יוהרא there.

keyTerms.meaning: we are witnesses, meaning it is obvious to all
the one who sees / an onlooker

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers to the contradiction. רבי יוחנן switches the names. רב שישא keeps the names and explains that יוהרא depends on how the act looks to onlookers. For the רבנן, the question is whether it stands out. For רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, the question is whether it looks like fake piety.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel

phrases.aramaic: אַדְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל לָא קַשְׁיָא:
phrases.english: against Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel is not difficult:
There (the groom), the matter depends on concentration,

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲנַן סָהֲדֵי דְּלָא מָצֵי לְכַוּוֹנֵי דַּעְתֵּיהּ.
phrases.english: and we all can testify that he cannot focus his mind.
But here (Tisha B'Av), someone who sees him says:
It is just that he has no work.

phrases.aramaic: פּוּק חֲזִי כַּמָּה בַּטְלָנֵי אִיכָּא בְּשׁוּקָא.
phrases.english: Go out and see how many idle people there are in the marketplace.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אַדְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב שישא's answer by resolving the second half of the double contradiction.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל worries about יוהרא for the חתן but not on תשעה באב, so he seems inconsistent.
steps.terutzMaskana: The חתן obviously cannot have כוונה, so his reading looks like fake piety. An idle person on תשעה באב just looks like someone without a job.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק היה קורא
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula marks the end of the second chapter of ברכות, פרק היה קורא.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק היה קורא.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the traditional line said at the end of a chapter. It marks that פרק היה קורא is finished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No argument happens here. It is a closing marker that expresses our wish to come back and learn this chapter again.

keyTerms.meaning: the name of the chapter (from its first words)

phrases.english: We will return to you, Hayah Korei.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter after the final discussion.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The second chapter of ברכות is complete.

steps.title: New chapter: an אונן is exempt from מצוות
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה rules that someone whose dead relative lies before him, not yet buried, is exempt from קריאת שמע, תפלה, תפילין, and all the מצוות of the Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One whose dead relative lies before him is exempt from קריאת שמע, from תפלה, from תפילין, and from all the מצוות stated in the תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new chapter begins with a new משנה. It teaches that a mourner before the burial is exempt from מצוות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While his relative is still unburied, the person is busy with the burial, so the Torah frees him from other obligations. The exemption is broad. It covers קריאת שמע, תפלה, תפילין, and every מצוה in the Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: one whose dead relative lies before him (not yet buried)
the leather boxes with פסוקים worn on the arm and head

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the opening rule of פרק מי שמתו. It is the source for the halachic status of an אונן, and the rest of the chapter builds on it.

phrases.english: Mishnah: One whose dead relative lies before him
is exempt from the reading of Shema,
from prayer, and from tefillin,
and from all the מצוות stated in the Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new chapter with a new topic after the הדרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone whose dead relative is not yet buried is exempt from קריאת שמע, תפלה, תפילין, and all מצוות in the Torah.

steps.title: Pallbearers: who is exempt and who is obligated
steps.stepSummary: Pallbearers who have not carried yet and are still needed are exempt from קריאת שמע. Those who already carried are obligated, even if they are still needed. Everyone is exempt from תפלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The people carrying the bier, their replacements, and the replacements of their replacements. Some are in front of the bier and some are behind it. Those in front who are still needed are exempt. Those behind, even if they are still needed, are obligated. Both groups are exempt from תפלה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues the rule about a מת and now turns to the people who carry the bier. It tells us which of them must say קריאת שמע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pallbearers took turns carrying the bier. 'In front of the bier' means people who have not had their turn yet, so they are still busy with the מצוה. 'Behind the bier' means people who already had their turn, so they are obligated in שמע. Since all of them are distracted, none of them can daven תפלה properly, so all are exempt from it.

keyTerms.meaning: Their replacements, who take over the carrying

steps.confusionAlert: 'Before' and 'after' the bier are not just about where people walk. 'Before' means those who have not yet taken their turn carrying, and 'after' means those who already carried. That turn is what decides whether they must say קריאת שמע.

phrases.english: The bier carriers and their replacements,
and the replacements of their replacements,
those before the bier,
phrases.notes: Those who have not carried yet

phrases.english: and those after the bier.

phrases.aramaic: אֶת שֶׁלִּפְנֵי הַמִּטָּה צוֹרֶךְ בָּהֶם — פְּטוּרִין,
phrases.english: Those before the bier who are needed are exempt,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֶת שֶׁלְּאַחַר הַמִּטָּה צוֹרֶךְ בָּהֶם — חַיָּיבִין.
phrases.english: while those after the bier, even if needed, are obligated.
Both these and those are exempt from prayer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the exemption from the relative of the מת to the people who carry the bier.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Pallbearers who are still needed and have not carried yet are exempt from שמע. Those who already carried are obligated. All are exempt from תפלה.

steps.title: Returning from the burial: begin שמע only if you can finish
steps.stepSummary: After the burial, people should start שמע only if they can finish it before reaching the mourners' row.
steps.simpleTranslation: They buried the dead and came back. If they can start and finish before they reach the row, they should start. If not, they should not start.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to the people walking back after the burial. It tells them when to begin קריאת שמע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'row' (שורה) is the line people form to comfort the mourners as they pass by. Comforting the mourners takes priority. So a person should not start שמע if he would have to stop in the middle when he reaches the row.

keyTerms.meaning: The row of people formed to comfort the mourners

phrases.english: If they buried the dead and returned,
if they are able to begin and finish
before they reach the row, they should begin.
And if not, they should not begin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves forward in time, from carrying the bier to returning after the burial.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Start שמע only if there is time to finish it before reaching the row.

steps.title: The mourners' row: inner line exempt, outer line obligated
steps.stepSummary: Those standing in the inner line, who actually comfort the mourners, are exempt from שמע. Those in the outer line are obligated.
steps.simpleTranslation: Those standing in the row: the inner ones are exempt, and the outer ones are obligated.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now rules about the people standing in the comforting row itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The inner line faces the mourners directly and does the comforting, so they are busy with a מצוה and are exempt. The outer line is there only to show respect and is not actually comforting anyone, so they must say שמע.

keyTerms.meaning: The inner ones, who face the mourners directly

phrases.english: Those standing in the row,
the inner ones are exempt,
and the outer ones are obligated.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues from the walk back to the row the returning people reach.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the row, the inner line is exempt from שמע and the outer line is obligated.
steps.whatToRemember: There is one principle behind the whole funeral section: you are exempt only while you are actually doing the funeral מצוה. Once you are not actively involved, you are obligated.

steps.title: Women, slaves, and minors: exemptions and obligations
steps.stepSummary: נשים, עבדים, and קטנים are exempt from קריאת שמע and תפילין. They are obligated in תפלה, מזוזה, and ברכת המזון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Women, slaves, and minors are exempt from קריאת שמע and from תפילין. They are obligated in prayer, in מזוזה, and in ברכת המזון.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to a new topic: which מצוות apply to women, slaves, and minors.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the exemption is not about being busy with something else. It depends on the type of מצוה (for example, time-bound מצוות). It lists two exemptions and three obligations. The גמרא will explain each one later.
steps.confusionAlert: This is a new rule. These exemptions are not about being busy or distracted, the way the funeral exemptions were.

phrases.english: Women, slaves, and minors
are exempt from the recitation of Shema and from tefillin,
and are obligated in prayer, mezuzah, and grace after meals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from exemptions caused by being busy to exemptions based on who the person is.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: נשים, עבדים, and קטנים are exempt from שמע and תפילין, but obligated in תפלה, מזוזה, and ברכת המזון.

steps.title: The גמרא infers from 'laid out before him'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads the משנה's words closely: only when the מת is lying in front of him is he exempt. When it is not, he is not exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: When the dead is laid out before him, yes, he is exempt. When it is not laid out before him, no, he is not exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by drawing an inference from the משנה's wording. This is a setup line that prepares the next move, a contradiction from another source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said 'מתו מוטל לפניו.' The גמרא understands those words as a limit: the exemption applies only when the body is physically in front of him. This inference will soon be tested against a ברייתא that seems to say something different.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Laid out before him, yes,
but not laid out before him, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: מוּטָּל לְפָנָיו — אִין, וְשֶׁאֵינוֹ מוּטָּל לְפָנָיו — לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the opening words of the משנה from step 19 and reads them closely.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: By inference: the exemption applies only when the מת is physically before him.
steps.whyThisMatters: This inference sets the terms for the coming challenge about whether an אונן is exempt even when the body is not in front of him.

steps.title: A contradiction: the mourner is exempt even when the body is not in front of him
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the close reading from step 24 with a ברייתא. The ברייתא lets the mourner eat in another room or a friend's house, yet he still does not say a ברכה or join a זימון.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they raised a contradiction: Someone whose dead relative is lying before him eats in a different room. If he has no other room, he eats in his friend's house. If he has no friend's house, he puts up a partition and eats. If he has nothing to make a partition with, he turns his face away and eats. He does not recline while eating. He does not eat meat or drink wine. He does not say a ברכה, and he does not join a זימון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge what it just learned from the משנה. The ברייתא shows the mourner is still exempt from ברכות even when he eats somewhere else, away from the body.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 24 said: only when the מת is in front of him is he exempt, but not otherwise. The ברייתא says that even in another room or another house he does not say a ברכה or make a זימון, so he is still exempt. That means the exemption does not depend on the body being physically in front of him, and this clashes with step 24.

keyTerms.meaning: And they raised a contradiction: a source is brought that seems to clash with what was just said
Another room or house, away from the body
Reclining while eating, the way people sat at an important, festive meal
Saying a ברכה, here the ברכות on food
Joining a זימון, the invitation to say ברכת המזון together as a group

steps.confusionAlert: In the ברייתא, the words 'מתו מוטל לפניו' cannot literally mean 'in front of him', because the same ברייתא sends him to another room or another house. Here the phrase simply describes a person whose dead is not yet buried. That gap between the literal words and how the ברייתא uses them is exactly what creates the contradiction.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the question of what really makes a mourner exempt: is it physically seeing the body, or simply that he is busy with an unburied relative? How the גמרא answers this decides how far the exemption reaches.

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction:
phrases.notes: Signals that a source is coming that seems to clash with the previous step.

phrases.english: One whose dead relative is lying before him
phrases.notes: Here it means someone whose relative has died and is not yet buried.

phrases.english: eats in another room,
phrases.notes: First choice: get away from the body.

phrases.english: and if he has no other room,
he eats in his friend's house,
and if he has no friend's house,
he makes a partition and eats,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם אֵין לוֹ דָּבָר לַעֲשׂוֹת מְחִיצָּה —
phrases.english: and if he has nothing to make a partition with,
he turns his face away and eats.
phrases.notes: Last option: at least don't face the body.

phrases.english: And he does not recline and eat.
phrases.notes: Reclining is a sign of a festive meal.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵינוֹ אוֹכֵל בָּשָׂר וְאֵינוֹ שׁוֹתֶה יַיִן,
phrases.english: And he does not eat meat and does not drink wine,
and he does not say a blessing, and he does not join a zimmun.
phrases.notes: This is the key line for the contradiction: he is exempt even when eating away from the body.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly challenges the close reading of the משנה made in step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference from step 24 that the mourner is exempt only when the מת is physically in front of him.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא has the mourner eat in another room or a friend's house, where the body is not in front of him, yet he still does not say a ברכה or make a זימון. So the exemption applies even when the body is not before him, which contradicts step 24.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the ברייתא, a mourner whose dead is not yet buried eats away from the body, avoids festive behavior (reclining, meat, wine), and is exempt from ברכות and זימון.
